documents.title: Neurology visit last month
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Kristen, Dennis's daughter, writing on his account. We saw neurology on January 19. They did another head CT and said there are many small old strokes and that his memory problem is now vascular dementia, not just the fluid. They told him no more driving, because he got lost several times last fall coming home from the store. He is upset about the car. They said they'd send you the notes. Do we need to change anything?

documents.title: RE: Neurology visit last month
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kristen, thank you for letting me know, and I'm sorry, that's a hard visit. I haven't received their note yet; we'll request it today. I agree with the driving advice. No medicine changes for now. Let's get him in next month so we can go over it together, and bring his pill box.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: vascular dementia per neurology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife and daughter. Per family, neurology in January diagnosed vascular dementia on a new CT showing multiple small strokes, and advised him to stop driving after he got lost several times. Their letter still not received; second request faxed today. He has handed over the car keys, reluctantly. More trouble planning his day, more confused. Wife now gives all medications again.
Exam: vitals as charted. Oriented to person and place, not date. Walker gait, slow. Right arm swings less than left.
A/P:
1. Vascular dementia (per neurology, pending letter): added to problem list. Safety at home, supervision of meds and finances. Caregiver resources given to Kristen.
2. Secondary prevention: continue aspirin, atorvastatin, BP meds.
3. BMP today. RTC June for diabetes.

reports.text:
Indication: progressive memory loss, executive dysfunction.
Technique: Noncontrast axial CT of the head.
Findings: Multiple small hypodense foci in the subcortical white matter of both cerebral hemispheres and in both basal ganglia. Ventricles enlarged, similar to the prior study. No acute hemorrhage, mass, or territorial infarct. No extra-axial collection.
reports.conclusion: Multiple small subcortical white matter and bilateral basal ganglia hypodensities, consistent with small vessel ischemic change. Stable ventriculomegaly.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up, 01/19/2024 (received 04/22)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — Follow-up, 01/19/2024
(Received after third request.)
Returns with daughter. Over the past year, progressive forgetfulness and difficulty organizing and planning daily tasks, which the family says is unlike him. He acknowledges feeling more muddled and has lost his way driving on several occasions. Background: prior TIA, CKD, cervical spondylotic myelopathy and normal pressure hydrocephalus (tap test with modest response, no shunt).
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs, morphine ER 60 mg BID, morphine IR 15 mg prn, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics, iodinated contrast.
Vitals: BP 145/90.
Lab: fasting glucose 162.
Exam: Drift of the right arm on pronator testing. Right-sided reflexes brisker than left. Slow gait with less arm swing on the right.
CT head without contrast: report attached.
Impression: Vascular dementia.
Plan: Stop driving. Vascular risk control with PCP. Home safety and caregiver support. Follow-up 1 year.
Neurologist

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Neurology letter came in April: matches what family told us. Not driving. Snacking more in the afternoons.
Exam: vitals as charted. Feet: no lesions.
Plan: A1c, urine albumin, lipids, BMP. Meal structure discussed with wife.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.6, up from 7.2. Urine albumin/creatinine 1,100 mg/g. Kidney function stable. For someone with dementia, 7.6 is acceptable; I'd rather avoid lows than add another pill. Recheck in the fall.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER — Follow-up, 06/28/2024
WM with AL lambda amyloidosis, ongoing very good partial response, no therapy since 2021. Family reports vascular dementia diagnosed by neurology.
Labs: hemoglobin 13.0; light chains remain low and stable.
Plan: observation every 6 months. Continue furosemide.
Hematology-oncology physician

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife. Since summer he has insisted on filling and taking his own pill box again; wife lets him to keep the peace and checks on it 'when I can.' Needs help bathing. Walker always. No falls. PHQ-9 5.
Advance care plan reviewed; proxy unchanged.
Safety: shower chair, grab bars in place.
Exam: as charted.
Vaccines next month: flu, COVID, RSV.
Labs today.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high-dose) L deltoid, COVID (Moderna updated) R deltoid, RSV L deltoid lower site. Wife consented with pt. Observed, tolerated.

documents.title: Pain management follow-up
documents.author: pain management
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PAIN MANAGEMENT CLINIC — Follow-up, 10/18/2024
Lumbar spinal stenosis; also cervical myelopathy, NPH and vascular dementia per records. Seen with wife, who reports pain stable. Regimen unchanged: morphine ER 60 mg q12h, morphine IR 15 mg q4h prn. Wife holds and dispenses the morphine. Monitoring program reviewed. Return 3 months.
Pain management physician

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re missed visit 12/9. Wife says they mixed up the date and the roads were icy. Rebooked 1/21 at 10:00. Reminder call set.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / HTN follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. He says he takes all his pills; he does his own box. Wife not sure. No headaches, no chest pain.
O: BP high today, repeated after rest, still up. Heart regular, no edema.
A/P: BP above goal and A1c drawn. Before adding anything, asked wife to take back the pill box and to bring all bottles next visit for a count. Recheck BP in 6-8 weeks. Will call with A1c.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 8.3, up from 7.6. Likely adherence; spoke with wife, who will supervise. Recheck BP and sugars at March visit.

reports.text:
Indication: acute involuntary movements of left arm and leg.
Technique: Noncontrast axial CT of the head.
Findings: Small area of hyperdensity in the deep structures of the right cerebral hemisphere. Multiple small chronic hypodensities in the subcortical white matter and both basal ganglia, unchanged. Enlarged ventricles, unchanged. No hemorrhage elsewhere, no mass effect, no extra-axial collection.
reports.conclusion: Small right deep hemispheric hyperdensity, consistent with acute lacunar infarct. Chronic small vessel changes and ventriculomegaly unchanged.

documents.title: Emergency department record, 03/29/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — Physician record, 03/29/2025 (received 04/03/2025)
CC: involuntary flinging movements, left side.
HPI: 74M with cervical spondylotic myelopathy, Waldenström macroglobulinemia and vascular dementia, brought by his wife after large, unpredictable flinging movements of the left arm and leg began earlier today and worsened through the afternoon; unable to walk or feed himself. Never had anything like this before. Hypertension and diabetes, both poorly controlled; reports not taking lisinopril or metformin for several months.
Home meds per list: HCTZ 12.5 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, morphine ER 60 mg BID, morphine IR 15 mg prn, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg; lisinopril and metformin prescribed but not taken.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis) — no CT angiography.
Exam: Alert and oriented. Continuous, irregular, large-amplitude movements of the left arm and leg. Tone hard to judge with the movements; no spasticity or rigidity. Reflexes symmetric. No pronator drift. Sensation intact. Cranial nerves intact.
Fingerstick glucose 214.
Noncontrast head CT: report attached.
Impression: Left hemiballism (chorea) from acute right lacunar infarct.
Disposition: Admitted to the hospital medicine service with neurology consultation.
ED physician

documents.title: Home physical therapy discharge summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
HOME HEALTH PHYSICAL THERAPY — Discharge summary
9 visits 04/10-05/15/2025. Diagnosis: right lacunar infarct with left hemiballism, vascular dementia, chronic gait disorder.
Progress: involuntary left arm movements now rare and small; transfers with supervision; ambulates household distances with rolling walker and standby assist. Caregiver trained in safe transfers.
Recommendations: continue home exercise program with wife; supervision for all walking.
Physical therapist

reports.text:
Indication: acute right-sided weakness.
Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without contrast, including diffusion-weighted imaging.
Findings: Small focus of restricted diffusion in a deep location, consistent with an acute lacunar infarct. Chronic small vessel changes in the subcortical white matter and basal ganglia. Ventriculomegaly, unchanged. No hemorrhage, mass or extra-axial collection.
reports.conclusion: Small acute lacunar infarct. Chronic small vessel disease and stable ventriculomegaly.

documents.title: Emergency department record, 03/20/2026
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — Physician record, 03/20/2026 (received 03/24/2026)
CC: sudden right-sided weakness.
History: 75M with WM, AL amyloidosis, NPH, vascular dementia, prior right lacunar infarct with left hemiballism (2025), HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a.
Home meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, morphine ER 60 mg BID, morphine IR 15 mg prn, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Exam: Weakness of the right face, arm and leg, equally reduced in proximal and distal muscles. Sensation, coordination, language and cranial nerves otherwise normal.
MRI brain: small lacunar infarct (report attached).
Impression: Acute lacunar infarct with pure motor right hemiparesis.
Disposition: ED observation overnight; therapy evaluation; discharged home 03/21 with home PT and PCP follow-up.
ED physician

8 visits since 03/30. Right-sided strength improving; ambulates 40 ft with rolling walker and contact guard. Transfers with minimal assist. Wife trained. Plan: 4 more weeks, then home program.
Physical therapist
